# Lab 2 - published checks (Tier A)

These are the checks `itsmlab verify 2` runs; the grader runs the same checker on the receipted
commit, and then re-derives every number on a fixture you have never seen. Bundles: **Core** is
pass/fail as a whole (every Core spec must pass; L2-CORE-6 is checked by the grader and shown as
`skip` locally), **Stretch** passes at any two of three, and the reasoning in `EDGE-CASES.md` and
your gaming write-up is read by the lecturer. Ids are stable.

Every rule id below (`R-nn`) is defined in `METRIC-SPEC.md`. The rules are published in full; only
the graded fixture's data is withheld. When a check fails on the graded run, the grader names the
field and the rule involved and never the expected value.

Fixture calls (creating the tickets check 2.12 needs, posting a log to your endpoint) are not
checks: when one fails, every check that depends on it is reported as `error` with the request and
response in the message.

Limits: `docker compose --profile tests build` is untimed in Tier A and killed after 300 s in
Tier B; `docker compose up --wait svcdesk` and `GET /health` have 120 s together; every request to
`POST /dora/metrics` has 30 s.

## L2-CORE-1 `compose-up` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L2-CORE-1.01 | compose file defines service svcdesk with build | a compose file exists at the repo root (discovery order `compose.yaml`, `compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yaml`, the first found wins, plus the matching `*.override.*` file if present) and defines a service `svcdesk` with a `build:` key (an `image:`-only service fails) |
| L2-CORE-1.02 | no host-path bind mounts | in the resolved configuration (`docker compose config --format json` over the same file list used for `up`) no service volume has `type: bind` and no top-level volume uses `driver_opts` with `type: none` or `o` containing `bind`; named volumes and `tmpfs` are fine |
| L2-CORE-1.03 | compose up --wait svcdesk within 120 s | after an untimed `docker compose build`, `docker compose up --wait svcdesk` succeeds within 120 s |
| L2-CORE-1.04 | GET /health answers 200 within 120 s | `GET /health` answers 200 within the same 120 s window |

## L2-CORE-2 `dora-api` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L2-CORE-2.01 | POST /dora/metrics answers with the full metric object | `POST /dora/metrics` with the practice fixture and the published window returns 200, `application/json`, and every key the response shape requires |
| L2-CORE-2.02 | the response echoes the window | `window.from` and `window.to` equal the request's, as instants |
| L2-CORE-2.03 | spec_version | `spec_version` is the string `1.0.0` |
| L2-CORE-2.04 | the endpoint is a pure function | the same request sent twice answers identically, field by field |
| L2-CORE-2.05 | order independence | the same events in reversed order answer identically, field by field |
| L2-CORE-2.06 | duplicate events are ingested once | every event duplicated answers identically, field by field |
| L2-CORE-2.07 | an empty log | 200; frequency 0.0; both medians and both ratios `null`; every count and anomaly 0 |
| L2-CORE-2.08 | an empty window is rejected | a window whose `to` is not after its `from` returns 400 or 422 with a top-level `error` |
| L2-CORE-2.09 | a missing window is rejected | a body without `window` returns 400 or 422 with a top-level `error` |
| L2-CORE-2.10 | missing or non-array events are rejected | a body whose `events` is absent, or is not an array, returns 400 or 422 |
| L2-CORE-2.11 | a malformed log is rejected | a log whose `reverts` names a sha that is not in the log returns 400 or 422 |
| L2-CORE-2.12 | GET /dora/ticket-events | 200 and an array; the three tickets the checker created are present with their `created` events, the stream is ordered by (`at`, `ticket_id`) ascending, and a ticket driven to `resolved` carries exactly the phases created, acknowledged, resolved |

## L2-CORE-5 `gaming` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L2-CORE-5.01 | gaming/after.jsonl is a well-formed log | `gaming/after.jsonl` exists, every line parses as JSON, and your service accepts it |
| L2-CORE-5.02 | gaming.json structure | `gaming.json` carries `metric`, `rule`, `before` and `after`; `metric` is one of the five metric field names and `rule` matches `R-\d\d` |
| L2-CORE-5.03 | R-19 conservation | in `after.jsonl` every base commit and incident is unchanged, and every base deployment keeps its id, outcome and environment and never moves earlier |
| L2-CORE-5.04 | the declared `before` is your service's own answer | `gaming.json`'s `before` equals your service's answer for the practice fixture, within R-18 |
| L2-CORE-5.05 | the declared `after` is your service's own answer | `gaming.json`'s `after` equals your service's answer for `gaming/after.jsonl` over the same window, within R-18 |
| L2-CORE-5.06 | R-20 improvement | at least one of the five metrics clears its published margin in the improving direction, and the metric named in `gaming.json` is one of them |
| L2-CORE-5.07 | R-21 harm | measured on the base work alone, the true change lead time is at least 125 % of the base's or the number of changes delivered is at most 90 % of the base's |

## L2-CORE-6 `prediction-order` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L2-CORE-6.01 | the prediction was receipted before the feature | when `PREDICTION.md` exists, a prediction receipt (`itsmlab submit 2 --kind prediction`) exists whose payload hash equals the sha256 of the committed file or of its front matter and whose `main` SHA is an ancestor of the submission commit; when it is absent both checks pass. A prediction the grader cannot confirm fails L2-STRETCH-1, not Core; deleting `PREDICTION.md` withdraws it |
| L2-CORE-6.02 | the feature's commits descend from the receipt | every commit touching the path named by `feature_path` is a descendant of the receipted SHA, except commits another lab's submission receipt bound; the local `skip` lists the commits that already touch it |
